concerns.text: The project's primary scientific contribution (Constitution Principle VI: ΔR² information loss, SC-002) and the entire scientific training/evaluation run are not executable — no verified dataset with formula/band_gap/hardness/crystal_system exists and the structure-aware baseline is unavailable. The plan honestly flags this, but as planned it can only deliver a tested pipeline with zero scientific results; the research question cannot be answered. This requires scope revision (new verified dataset or reframed question) before the plan is scientifically sound, not just a limitation note.

Interpretability validation is quasi-circular: PCs are correlated with 'atomic mass, melting point, bulk modulus'. Atomic mass is essentially a monotone function of atomic number, an input node feature — a significant correlation is near-guaranteed by construction, not evidence of meaningful learning. Bulk modulus is physically the basis of the hardness training target, so correlating embeddings with it is close to validating against the label. Choose genuinely held-out properties (e.g., thermal conductivity, sound velocity) or drop atomic mass.

The composition 'graph' is fully-connected with edge weights computed as Euclidean distance in the SAME 4-D property space used for node features. The graph therefore carries no information beyond the node features (it is a deterministic function of them), and standard GCNConv ignores edge_weight unless explicitly wired. The GNN-vs-RF comparison is still valid, but the plan should acknowledge the graph adds no compositional information (e.g., stoichiometry is only weakly encoded via pooling) — otherwise the 'graph representation' framing overstates what is tested.

'95% prediction intervals as mean ± 1.96 × std of fold predictions' is not a prediction interval for a new material — fold-to-fold model variance does not capture residual/aleatoric error, so the interval will be far too narrow. Either rename it a fold-uncertainty band or compute a proper prediction interval (e.g., conformal or residual-based).

The claim 'detecting ΔR² ≈ 0.05 ... power > 0.80 at α = 0.05, Cohen 1988 conventions' is asserted without a test, effect-size metric, or dependence structure (paired folds). Either state the power analysis will be computed at run time with the actual fold-level ΔR² values (e.g., paired t-test across folds) or remove the numeric claim.
